items.title: IPCC Opens Sixty Fifth Plenary Session in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
items.description: ADDIS ABABA, Oct 12 – The Sixty-Fifth Session of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) began today in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. IPCC member governments are meeting from 12 to 16 October to advance the IPCC work planned for the seventh assessment cycle. The Panel’s agenda for this session includes several important topics, led by […]

items.title: UN carbon market forces cookstove projects to protect against forest loss
items.description: Despite lobbying for an exemption, the UN regulator has for the first time made cookstove projects cover the risk that the trees they save are later destroyed The post UN carbon market forces cookstove projects to protect against forest loss appeared first on Climate Home News.

items.title: Germany news: Economy set for stronger growth, wine harvest hit by drought
items.description: Germany's economic outlook is looking a little brighter, with the International Monetary Fund almost doubling its growth forecast. However, Germany's winegrowers are facing another disappointing harvest. DW has more.

items.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
items.description: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s" continuing the country’s investment in international sport.

items.title: Bulgaria condemns Black Sea drone attacks as Russia's war in Ukraine spills over into Eastern Europe
items.description: Bulgaria has seen the second spate of drone attacks on merchant ships off its coast in the past week. Russia has been accused of repeatedly targeting civilian cargo ships in the area.

items.title: What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?
items.description: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.

items.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
items.description: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.
